newsitem.title: CHINA: Danfoss plans $22.5 mln north China plant.
newsitem.headline: Danfoss plans $22.5 mln north China plant.

text.p: Danfoss Group of Denmark said on Friday it will build a new $22.5 million plant in the north China city of Tianjin aimed at meeting growing demand for energy saving heating and water control equipment.

Danfoss expects the facility, which will produce radiator thermostats, thermostatic expansion valves and water control valves, to help boost its sales in China to $50 million a year by 2000 from about $10 million last year, company president Joergen Clausen told reporters.
The privately held company with world sales of about $2 billion last year plans to break ground on the plant in Tianjin's Wuqing Development Zone on Saturday with completion expected in 1999.
Clausen said home heating is expected to be a major source of new demand for the company as China installs more energy efficient heating control systems in its residential housing.
The new wholly owned plant will export some of its output, he added.
Danfoss currently manufactures its products at a smaller site it leases in Tianjin.
